previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old female with a history of type I diabetes, end-stage renal disease with prior kidney and pancreas transplants, and severe mitral regurgitation was admitted for worsening heart failure symptoms, primarily fatigue and dyspnea. She underwent elective cardiac catheterization, which revealed two-vessel coronary artery disease with a 90% proximal LAD stenosis and 80% RCA lesions, confirming chronic inferior ischemia as the cause of her mitral regurgitation. Due to the extent of disease, she was scheduled for coronary artery bypass grafting and mitral valve replacement. Her renal function remained stable with protective hydration, and no dialysis was required. She was discharged home with medication adjustments, including increased aspirin and reduced ranitidine, and instructions to monitor weight and prepare for upcoming surgery.

Conclusions  
PRE-BYPASS: 
The left atrium is dilated. No spontaneous echo contrast or 
thrombus is seen in the body of the left atrium/left atrial 
appendage or the body of the right atrium/right atrial 
appendage. A patent foramen ovale is present. A left-to-right 
shunt across the interatrial septum is seen at rest.

Left ventricular wall thicknesses and cavity size are normal. 
There is moderate to severe regional left ventricular systolic 
dysfunction with akinetic/aneurysmal basal inferior and basal 
inferoseptal walls. The mid and apical inferior, inferoseptal 
walls are severe. Overall left ventricular systolic function is 
moderately depressed (LVEF= 35% %). 

The right ventricular cavity is dilated with mild global free 
wall hypokinesis. 

There are simple atheroma in the ascending aorta. There is a 
ridge of calcium/tissue in the ST junction, with a small mobile 
atheroma. This point seems to be cause of increased transaortic 
velocity of 1.7 m/sec, The velocity at the aortic valve seems 
normal. There are simple atheroma in the descending thoracic 
aorta. 

The aortic valve leaflets (3) are mildly thickened but aortic 
stenosis is not present. No aortic regurgitation is seen. 

The mitral valve leaflets are mildly thickened. Moderate to 
severe (3+) mitral central regurgitation is seen. There is no 
prolapse or flail mitral leaflets. The vena contract measures 
upto 6mm.

There is no pericardial effusion.

patient was evaluated by the physical therapy service for

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ woman status post CABG and mitral valve replacement.
Assess for pneumothorax and line placement.

COMPARISON:  Pre-operative chest radiograph on ___.

SINGLE SUPINE PORTABLE CHEST RADIOGRAPH:  The endotracheal tube terminates 3.7
cm above the carina.  The Swan-Ganz catheter via right IJ approach terminates
in the right main pulmonary artery.  A left-sided chest tube terminates in the
lateral base.  NG tube is seen in the stomach with the tip excluded from the
radiograph.  Two mediastinal drains terminate in the mid thoracic level. 
External cardiac pacers are noted in the left upper abdomen.  

The lungs are symmetric in volumes, but with mild hazy opacities, compatible
with non-full expansion and/or mild pulmonary edema.  There is no mediastinal
shift, pneumothorax, pleural effusion or focal air-space consolidation. 
Multilevel median sternotomy wires are intact.  

IMPRESSION:  No pneumothorax, pleural effusions, or acute surgical
complications.  Support devices in standard positions.

CHEST X-RAY

HISTORY:  Line placement.

One portable view.  Comparison with the previous study done ___. 
Prominent interstitial markings consistent with mild edema persist.  There is
evidence of a right pleural effusion which may have increased.  There is new
subsegmental atelectasis at the left base.  The patient is status post median
sternotomy, CABG and MVR as before.  Mediastinal structures are unchanged.  An
endotracheal tube, nasogastric tube, left chest tube, mediastinal drains and
Swan-Ganz catheter have been withdrawn.  A right internal jugular line has
been placed, terminating at the cavoatrial junction.

IMPRESSION:  Line placement as described.
